data.title: Disabled
data.tagline: Show that a control is currently unavailable
data.description: A disabled control cannot be operated in the current state. Use it when the action is visible and its future availability matters, and explain what condition is missing. If the action is irrelevant, removing it may be clearer than leaving a page full of disabled controls.

use: Prevent submission until required input is present
Show an unavailable step that may become available
Block an action while the same request is running
Represent a permission or state constraint
avoid: Disable a control without explaining why
Use low contrast that makes the label unreadable
Leave keyboard focus on a control that cannot respond
Disable most of the page instead of clarifying the workflow

lessonPractice.title: Submit is disabled because Company name is empty, but people only see a gray button. How can the reason become clear?

options.label: Put the reason only in a mouse-hover tooltip on the button
options.feedback: Native disabled buttons are often not focusable, and touch has no reliable hover, so the reason remains inaccessible.

options.label: Explain the requirement near the missing field and update the button as it is completed
options.feedback: The cause and remedy appear where the problem occurs, and every input method can see when submission becomes available.

options.label: Lower the button opacity but still submit when it is clicked
options.feedback: The visual state says unavailable while the behavior still runs, creating conflicting feedback and incomplete submissions.

data.agentPrompt: When Submit is disabled because Company name is missing, explain the requirement near the field and update the button as input changes. Do not rely on a tooltip or gray styling while still submitting. Verify visible reasons and consistent behavior with keyboard and touch.
